correctness.rationale: For smooth ordered triples in F_{5^n} derive the three elliptic quotient Hasse polynomials, with Hr=r²−rst+s²t²+2s²+2t²+2; the prime-to-5 quotient isogeny transfers p-rank, a-number and Newton slopes to the three elliptic factors. Smooth U_q excludes r,s,t=±2 and Delta=4+rst−r²−s²−t²=0; quadratic-character summation yields |U_q|=q³−7q²+18q−17. The identities Hr+Delta=(s²+1)(t²+1), Hr−Hs=−(r²−s²)(t²+1), the Mobius transform of t and a²−2a−2=0 give intersection counts T1=q²−6q+10+(7−2q)eps, T2=2(q−4−eps), T3=4(1+eps). Explicit inclusion–exclusion yields all four N_f formulas for every n>=1; eight superspecial marked triples occur iff n even. Independent F5 and F25 field enumeration gave strata (0,12,0,11), (8,96,1110,10469) and T1/T2/T3=(8,4,0),(442,40,8), matching formulas. Finite tests are not proof of all extensions.
residual_risks: Nonisomorphism of marked triples is not asserted; no twist or automorphism quotient taken.
Superspecial finite set and all n are justified symbolically; finite q<=25 alone would not suffice.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: Ohashi supplies the Ciani elliptic quotient and superspecial structural theory; Lercier et al. study general moduli and prime >=11 class statistics. Neither inspected source states all marked coefficient triples by p-rank in characteristic five with parity corrections. Brock thesis was bibliographically noted but not read; it could overlap rank zero alone, not established to cover full four-rank census.
residual_risks: Brock 1993 complete thesis inaccessible and could cover the rank0 eight-point subset.
An unindexed marked p-rank census with equivalent Hasse equations may preexist.
Counts of isomorphism classes and marked triples cannot be conflated.

value.rationale: The Ciani genus-three family is a natural 3-parameter arithmetic family with three elliptic quotients. The all-extension marked four-stratum census, exact parity dependence, Newton-slope and a-number profile quantify every p-rank, whereas prior results emphasize superspecial loci or isomorphism tables. The closed character-sum formulas provide useful arithmetic distribution data, independent of a larger downstream theorem.
residual_risks: Restricted to characteristic five smooth normalized Ciani quartics, ordered coefficients; no moduli quotient or arbitrary p.

limitations: Not a count of isomorphism classes; F125 independently untested this run, although source reports a test.
